q: White light passes at a slant through a flat window pane of uniform thickness. Why does the window not visibly split the light into colours, even though glass has dispersion?
a: Inside the glass the colours travel in slightly different directions, but the surfaces of a pane of uniform thickness are parallel. At the second surface each colour is refracted back to a direction parallel to the original ray, so the colours continue in the same direction, only slightly shifted sideways. The slanted surfaces of a prism, by contrast, increase the difference in direction.

q: The sun shines from a height of $50^\circ$, and it is raining ahead. Can an observer standing on level ground see a rainbow?
a: No. The antisolar point is $50^\circ$ below the horizon, so the top of the red arc would be at a height of $42^\circ - 50^\circ = -8^\circ$, that is, below the horizon. A rainbow is seen from the ground only when the sun is lower than $42^\circ$.
